verses.text: Masters, give your slaves what is right and fair. You know that you also have a Master in heaven.
Keep on praying. Stay alert as you pray, and be thankful.
Pray for us too, that God will open a door for our message. Then we can preach the secret of Christ, which is why I am in chains.
Pray that I will make it clear, as I should.
Be wise in the way you act towards outsiders. Make the most of every chance.
Let your talk always be full of grace and tasty, as if seasoned with salt. Then you will know how to answer everyone.
Tychicus will tell you all my news. He is a dear brother, a faithful helper and a fellow servant in the Lord.
I am sending him to you for this very reason, so that you know how we are, and so that he can encourage your hearts.
He is coming with Onesimus, our faithful and dear brother, who is one of you. They will tell you everything that is happening here.
Aristarchus, who is in prison with me, sends greetings. So does Mark, the cousin of Barnabas. You have been told about him: if he comes to you, welcome him.
Jesus, who is called Justus, also sends greetings. These are the only Jewish believers among my co-workers for God's Kingdom. They have been a comfort to me.
Epaphras, who is one of you and a servant of Christ Jesus, sends greetings. He is always praying hard for you. He prays that you will stand firm, mature and fully sure of all that God wants.
I can tell you that he is working very hard for you, and for those in Laodicea and Hierapolis.
Our dear friend Luke, the doctor, and Demas send greetings.
Give my greetings to the brothers and sisters at Laodicea, and to Nympha and the church that meets in her house.
After this letter has been read to you, make sure it is also read in the church at Laodicea. And you must read the letter from Laodicea too.
Tell Archippus, "Make sure you finish the work the Lord gave you."
I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand. Remember my chains. Grace be with you.
